subject: On-prem K8s: inventory -> production handoff & storage policy decisions
messages:
From: Jared Price <jared.price@hollowsystems.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+deployments@hollowsystems.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hollow Systems — preflight inventory and storage constraints

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Ops wants to move from PoC to an initial production slice but we need to align on a few constraints before we schedule the onsite install:

- Inventory: We have 6 racks (36 nodes) across two rooms; 24 nodes have 8x NVMe each, 12 nodes boot off JBOD SAS with 2x NVMe cache.
- Network: Private L2 fabric with an eBGP edge; no public IPs for inference nodes — outbound NAT via edge.
- Storage policy: Customer wants short-term local caching + nightly push to central object store (S3-compatible) retained for 90 days.
- Encryption: They require CMEK (customer-managed keys) for persisted KV caches and any disk snapshots.

Attached is a quick inventory export. Can Redwood confirm whether the runtime supports:
1) mixed-node pool (NVMe + JBOD with cache) with per-node PV class mapping,
2) CMEK for local blockstore snapshots, and
3) a suggested eviction policy for prefix/KV caches?

We'd like a mutual action plan so procurement can start paperwork (timeline target: 45 days).

-Jared
Jared Price
Director, Platform Operations | Hollow Systems
ops@hollowsystems.com

Attachments: hollow_preflight_inventory.csv (CSV - 47KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Jared Price <jared.price@hollowsystems.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, ops+deployments@hollowsystems.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hollow Systems — preflight inventory and storage constraints

Jared — thanks for the inventory and clear asks. Short answers up front: yes / yes / yes (with recommendations). Below is a proposed plan and open questions.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Cluster topology: two logical clusters (prod-primary + prod-failover) mapped to the two rooms. Each cluster will have three node pools: compute-gpu (NVMe primaries), compute-cache (JBOD nodes with NVMe cache attached via local PV), and infra (control-plane, router, logging).
- PV classes: we recommend three StorageClasses: sc-nvme-fast (local NVMe, ephemeral + local cache), sc-jbod-hybrid (hostPath/CSI driver backed BFQ profile with cache tier), sc-blocksnap (for snapshotable encrypted block devices).
- CMEK: Redwood supports KMS integrations for snapshot encryption; we'll need the KMS endpoint and a service principal.
- Cache eviction: set prefix TTL 30–45 min for hot keys, persistent KV flush to object store every 4 hours, and nightly full checkpoint to S3 (90 day retention).

Open questions:
1) Can you confirm whether the JBOD nodes expose any local NVMe via PCI passthrough or are they only present as oob cache appliances?
2) Who owns the KMS tenant (Hollow or a partner)? We need credentials for a test key.
3) Any regulatory hold that prevents nightly checkpointing off-site?

Attached: redwood_onprem_checklist_v1.pdf and a draft MAP (MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v0.9.xlsx) — these contain the playbook, roles, and timeline. Please review.

Next steps:
- Laura to follow up with storage-class mapping and node affinity rules.
- Monica to kick off a small proof-of-concept for CMEK with a sample snapshot.
- Jared / Ops to confirm KMS ownership and JBOD access.

I'll propose slot options for a 60-minute design review next week once we get the KMS answer.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127

Attachments: redwood_onprem_checklist_v1.pdf (PDF - 320KB), MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v0.9.xlsx (XLSX - 58KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jared Price <jared.price@hollowsystems.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ops+deployments@hollowsystems.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hollow Systems — preflight inventory and storage constraints

Jared / team — quick technical clarifications from infra/storage before the review:

1) Node pool sizing: can you share typical sequence lengths and concurrent request estimates for the first 45-day window? That helps determine KV memory sizing and NVMe I/O QoS.
2) Block snapshot cadence: do you want application-consistent snapshots or crash-consistent is acceptable initially? App-consistent will add ~10–15% snapshot window.
3) Network egress: we recommend a dedicated egress VLAN for checkpoint traffic with QoS to avoid saturation of model-serving latency. Is that feasible on your fabric?

We propose these defaults unless you push back: 8GB KV per GPU host, snapshot cadence every 6 hours (crash-consistent initially), and checkpoint egress window between 02:00–05:00 local time.

Also uploading a small node IO profile graph we captured during the PoC. This helped us size ephemeral IO for the fastest pool.

-Laura Bennett
Principal Cloud Engineer — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: node_io_profile-20280710.png (PNG - 210KB)

From: Jared Price <jared.price@hollowsystems.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ops+deployments@hollowsystems.com, procurement@hollowsystems.com
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hollow Systems — preflight inventory and storage constraints

Thanks all — answers inline and a few asks: 

> 1) JBOD access:
JBOD nodes expose 2x NVMe each via PCI passthrough to the OS (we can present them as local devices). The 2x NVMe are intended primarily as cache; they are not mirrored.

> 2) KMS ownership:
Hollow controls the KMS tenant (AWS KMS in our case). We can provision a test CMK and provide an IAM role for Redwood to assume.

> 3) Regulatory hold:
No holds — S3-compatible object store is inside our DR region and is fine for 90-day retention. We do require audit logs for snapshot access.

Traffic/QoS: we can expose a dedicated egress VLAN and set DSCP for checkpoint flows — network team is on board.

Sequence/concurrency: expected median sequence length 256 tokens, 40 concurrent sessions in week 0 ramping to 120 over 45 days.

Snapshot consistency: crash-consistent initially is acceptable.

One procurement ask: can Redwood provide a bill-of-materials (HW & SW) and a rough monthly unit cost for the proposed topology so procurement can model the contract?

-Jared

Attachments: none

On Tue, Jul 10, 2028 at 09:14 AM Jared Price <jared.price@hollowsystems.com> wrote:
> (original inventory + asks)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Jared Price <jared.price@hollowsystems.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ops+deployments@hollowsystems.com, procurement@hollowsystems.com
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hollow Systems — preflight inventory and storage constraints

Jared — good to have answers, appreciate the speed. Attached is an updated mutual action plan and a short BOM + TCO sketch for the first tranche (attached). Highlights and next steps below: 

Highlights:
- Topology: we will map the two rooms to two K8s clusters behind the eBGP edge. Each cluster will host a primary GPU pool (24 NVMe hosts mapped to sc-nvme-fast), a cache pool (12 JBOD hosts mapped to sc-jbod-hybrid), and a small infra pool (3 control nodes + logging/egress).
- KMS/CMEK: Redwood will integrate with your AWS KMS CMK via an assumed IAM role. Monica will run a test-run for snapshot encryption in our staging tenant next week.
- Cache policy: prefix TTL 45 min, KV in-memory cap set to 12GB per GPU host for initial ramp; KV flush every 4 hours; checkpoint nightly 02:00–04:00 with DSCP tagging on the dedicated egress VLAN.
- Eviction: LRU with weighted cold-prefetch backfill to object-store on eviction.

Procurement/BOM: an estimated monthly unit cost and a HW bill-of-materials are attached (MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v0.9.xlsx includes price bands). Procurement — please flag any contractual minimums.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Monica Patel: validate CMK flow w/ a snapshot test in staging (due 2028-07-22).
- Laura Bennett: provide final StorageClass YAMLs and node-affinity snippets (due 2028-07-20).
- Hollow Ops (Jared): confirm final concurrency profile on 2028-07-20 and share IAM role ARN.
- Marissa Cole: start an SOW draft and send preliminary commercial terms to procurement (due 2028-07-24).

We can run the 60-minute design review Thursday 2028-07-20 at 10:00 PT if that works for all. I put a placeholder calendar invite.

DocuSign: once we agree on the MAP and SOW we can route the DocuSign envelope here: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-hollow-redwood-map

Thanks — looking forward to the review.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
